title: A Better Way to Give Feedback
attribution: Fictional scenario for development and testing, based on the supplied adapted rule excerpt. It is not official GitLab training or policy.

characters.name: Casey
characters.role: Teammate responsible for a delayed handoff
characters.personality: Busy and open to useful feedback

nodes.speaker: C1
nodes.narration: A project handoff arrived two days after the agreed time, delaying the next team's work. You want to raise the issue with Casey. What do you say?

choices.text: “Casey is careless and always slows everyone down.”
choices.consequence: The feedback labels Casey instead of describing the specific action or outcome, making it harder to discuss a constructive next step.

choices.text: “The handoff arrived two days after our agreed time, which delayed the next step. Can we work out what blocked it and agree on a plan?”
choices.consequence: You describe the outcome factually, focus on an action rather than a personal attribute, and invite a way forward.

choices.text: “No worries, everything is fine,” even though the delay affected the project.
choices.consequence: Avoiding the issue leaves the process bottleneck unclear and unresolved.

nodes.speaker: C2
nodes.narration: Casey says they were waiting for an input from another team, but no one knew the handoff was blocked. How do you respond?

choices.text: “Thanks for explaining. Let's note where the handoff got stuck and agree how to flag a blocker earlier next time.”
choices.consequence: You keep the discussion factual and focused on an actionable process improvement.

choices.text: “You should have figured it out yourself. You always make excuses.”
choices.consequence: The response makes a personal judgment rather than clarifying the specific blocker or a next step.

choices.text: “Let's not mention the delay. We can just keep hoping the handoff works next time.”
choices.consequence: The bottleneck remains hidden, so the team loses an opportunity to address it directly.

nodes.speaker: C1
nodes.narration: You are writing a short follow-up so you both remember the discussion. Which note is most useful?

choices.text: “The handoff was delayed while we waited for the other team's input. We agreed to flag blocked dependencies earlier and check the handoff date together.”
choices.consequence: The note describes the process issue factually and records a concrete next step without making it about someone's character.

choices.text: “Casey is unreliable and needs to care more about the team.”
choices.consequence: The note uses a personal label rather than describing the specific action, outcome, or change needed.
The note hides the delay and provides no information that could help resolve the bottleneck.

endings.title: Specific feedback, clear next step
endings.summary: You described the impact and agreed how to flag blockers earlier.
endings.feedback: Useful feedback focuses on specific actions or outcomes, describes process bottlenecks factually, and points toward a way forward.

reflection.prompt: What made your feedback easier to act on?

options.text: It described an observable outcome and a concrete next step.
It avoided mentioning the issue at all.

endings.title: Bring the feedback back to actions
endings.summary: The note focused on Casey's character instead of the handoff and its impact.
endings.feedback: Try describing the specific action or outcome, the effect it had, and a constructive next step. Keep the problem factual so it can be resolved.

reflection.prompt: How could you make the feedback more useful?

options.text: Replace the personal label with the delayed handoff, its impact, and an agreed next step.
Make the personal label sound more cheerful.

endings.title: Describe the bottleneck clearly
endings.summary: The follow-up did not record the delay or how to prevent the blocker next time.
endings.feedback: Factual feedback can name a problem without attacking a person. Clear information helps the team resolve process bottlenecks directly.

reflection.prompt: What should a useful follow-up include?

options.text: The observable delay and the step agreed to address it.
A positive statement that leaves out the problem.
